content:
Last month we ran a poll, and the overwhelming majority of 9to5Mac readers agreed that Apple should exit the advertising business.

Ads have now landed in Apple Maps in the US and Canada, and I think the situation is just as distasteful as you would imagine…

Apple telegraphed this back in March, saying that ads would appear in the Maps app at some point this summer. We finally got our first look at them yesterday, with Apple confirming that ads had begun rolling out over the past few days. All users in the US and Canada will see them over the coming weeks.

  • Before search: Sponsored suggestions will appear below the Featured Locations section on the search page.
  • After search: Ads will appear alongside relevant search results.

Apple says that privacy is one of their priorities.

I absolutely believe that, but for two reasons I still find the whole thing tacky.

John Atkinson’s featured comment:

The only non-ad-revenue reason I can think of for putting ads in Apple Maps is that it might encourage more businesses to claim their business pages. Apple Maps has never been able to catch up to Google Maps, and one long-running reason for that is that many businesses simply don’t want to take the time to add themselves to the map or keep their information from going stale. In North America, given iPhone penetration, this isn’t a big problem, but abroad it absolutely is.

In theory, ads could be an inducement for businesses to upload their information, since they can advertise all in the same app (or, to advertise, their marketing teams will have to fill out all the information). But I don’t think this is why Apple is doing it? Absolutely not — obviously it’s to make more money — but there is at least an ancillary benefit of potentially improving map data quality.

First, while Apple won’t serve you personalized ads via any form of tracking, virtually every other app and website does. The natural assumption will be that the iPhone maker does too — however unfair that perception — and that damages Apple’s reputation for protecting user privacy.

Second, it’s just so tacky. In the app and web publishing ecosystem, advertising is a necessary evil: it’s precisely because of ads that free apps or websites can continue to operate. But Apple absolutely does not need ad revenue to pay the rent: their premium hardware is priced plenty high enough already. Ads simply do not fit the Apple brand.

I recall John Gruber once compared ads in Apple apps to those obnoxious Intel Inside stickers on cheap Windows laptops. Of course we understand that the makers of cheap laptops need to chase every possible revenue source, but we never expected Apple to slap the same kind of sticker on a MacBook to debase the brand. How then can we accept ads in the native apps on Apple devices?

My position remains unchanged: Apple should not be in the advertising business at all.
